implementation_notes: TypeScript interfaces are structural, so LSP is not enforced unless the type carries a private or `unique symbol` brand. Put contracts in the consuming module, inject via constructor parameters, use `readonly` on public surfaces, and enable `noImplicitOverride` plus strict mode so substitutability regressions surface in CI.
idiom_name: structural interfaces with branded escape hatch + constructor injection
pitfalls: Structural typing means two unrelated shapes with the same members are interchangeable — that is a feature but it hides intent.
Parameter properties (`constructor(private x: T)`) couple the constructor signature to the field; it breaks substitutability of the constructor itself.
Interfaces declared alongside the implementation do not invert the dependency.
Type-only imports matter with `isolatedModules`; forgetting `import type` can create runtime cycles.
